title: Customer quote-access token stored and compared in plaintext (no hash at rest)
taxonomy: M1 — Insecure token storage / defense-in-depth gap
description: The public, unauthenticated quote-view/accept surface is gated by `quotes.customer_access_token`, a 256-bit random bearer token. It is minted with randomBytes(32).toString('base64url') and stored VERBATIM in the quotes table, then resolved by a direct plaintext equality lookup in the public accept route (public/quote/[token]/select/route.ts:28 `.eq('customer_access_token', token)`). Because the token is 256-bit it is not guessable, so this is not a Critical/High. But it is stored in cleartext alongside the data it protects, unlike the sibling public-chat surface which hashes its token (SHA-256) before storing/looking up (public/chat/[token]/route.ts:94-100, `sha256Hex(token)` against `public_access_token_hash`). A read-only breach of the quotes table (log dump, backup leak, SQL-read-only compromise) therefore yields directly-usable capability tokens that let an attacker view customer PII on the quote and flip the quote to 'accepted'. Hashing at rest would make a leaked column inert. Inconsistent with the codebase's own PAT handling (personal_access_tokens stores only token_hash — integrations/tokens/route.ts:101) and its public-chat token handling.
okWhen: The quotes table (and its backups/logs) is treated as a secrets store with the same at-rest controls as password hashes, AND the operational threat model accepts that a read-only DB exposure hands out live capability tokens. Also OK if there is an accepted-risk decision to keep quote tokens plaintext for support/debuggability.
notOkWhen: You want a leaked/backed-up quotes row to be inert (defense-in-depth against DB-read-only compromise), or you want token handling consistent with personal_access_tokens and the public-chat surface, both of which store only a SHA-256 hash. Fix: store sha256(token) in a customer_access_token_hash column and compare the hash, mirroring public-chat.
